findings.quote: I used v equal to gt for the fall
findings.note: The right route describes a wrong method: v = gt with the given final speed gives 1.8 s, which is option 3, not the 2.2 s answer. It is also the identical string used as mistakes[1].route, so the menu offers one phrase as both the right way and a wrong way - the student who used the average-speed method has no honest route to tap, and the student who used v = gt taps a phrase the menu scores as correct.
findings.fix: I divided the height by the average speed

notes: Recomputed: 20 divided by the mean of 0 and 18 gives 2.22, so 2.2 s is right; 18/10 = 1.8 s and the plain free-fall time 2 s reproduce the option-3 and option-4 entries, and both are correctly typed application with routes that describe their own entries. The option-2 distractor flag is honest (2.5 s would need a divisor of 8 that nothing here supplies). mistakes[1].route itself is fine - the defect is that right_route copies it.
